subject: St Martin's Hall / St Martin's Music Hall, 89 Long Acre, London
historical_event: Founding meeting of the International Working Men's Association, 28 September 1864

claims_used: Original site parcel approximately 149 by 61 ft
Great Hall intended at approximately 121 by 55 by 40 ft
Partially completed room opened in February 1850
Completed Great Hall: 121 ft 6 in by 55 ft 5 in by 40 ft
East-end platform, west-end gallery and galleries on part of the long sides
Flat central ceiling with sloped sides and timber panels
Two classrooms 31 by 19 ft and 26 by 19 ft
A corridor extended along the building
The full account also describes additional offices and rooms
The 1853 hall was later restored after fire and used as a music hall

model_method: Historical reconstruction at 0.1 model unit per foot. The Great Hall is on the upper level, using dimensions and spatial features described for the 1853 completed building; selected reported ground-level rooms are included. Their plan arrangement is schematic.
uncertainty: No verified complete 1853 floor plan has been located. Lower-floor room adjacencies, corridor and entrance-hall placements and stair geometry are schematic. The reported secretary office, ticket office and mezzanine ladies room are not yet modelled because reliable dimensions and plan locations are unavailable. Seating and people are not claimed to reproduce the 1864 event.
license: The project-authored geometry is an interpretive reconstruction based on cited historical text. Referenced archival engravings are linked separately with their own rights and credits; no unlicensed 1853 image has been copied into the project.
